page: Google Cloud Platform g2-standard-8 is a GPU-accelerated server configuration engineered for graphics workloads and artificial intelligence inference. The instance is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon processor operating at 2.2 GHz, providing 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core. Cache resources include 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and a shared 38 MB L3 cache, backed by instruction flags such as AVX-512 and AVX-512 VNNI. System memory totals 32.0 GB of RAM, yielding an even ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware acceleration is provided by a single NVIDIA L4 GPU from the Ada Lovelace architecture, featuring 24 GB of dedicated VRAM. The instance includes no bundled local storage and zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, relying entirely on network-attached storage and standard cloud networking.

Benchmark evaluation highlights substantial differentiation between the server's accelerator capabilities and host CPU performance. The presence of the NVIDIA L4 GPU drives top-tier performance for AI workloads, processing small (135M) model prompt ingestion at 11,784.81 tokens per second and text generation at 400.83 tokens per second. Medium (7B) model benchmarks achieve 2,225.82 tokens per second for prompt processing and 52.31 tokens per second during generation, both positioning within the top 10 percent of recorded results. In contrast, CPU-centric metrics register lower relative throughput. Single-core evaluations, including Geekbench (1,059.0) and stress-ng (1,200.99), place in the lower quartile, as do compilation and compression tasks. Multi-core execution and memory throughput align with mid-range tiers, marked by a PassMark CPU score of 7,244.68, uncached read bandwidth of 50.64 GB/sec, and Redis operations scaling to 6.2 million sets per second.

This hardware balance positions the g2-standard-8 as a cost-efficient deployment platform for targeted inference and accelerated visual compute rather than general-purpose CPU tasks. Because general CPU throughput is modest and local storage is omitted, deploying compute-heavy compile jobs or local disk-intensive tasks on this instance yields suboptimal resource efficiency. The architecture is best deployed for real-time machine learning inference, generative AI text generation on small-to-medium parameter models, audio and video transcoding, and GPU-driven graphics rendering where execution is predominantly offloaded to the Ada Lovelace accelerator.
description: Google Cloud Platform g2-standard-8 is a GPU-optimized instance featuring an x86_64 Intel Xeon processor with 8 vCPUs (4 physical cores) at 2.2 GHz, 32.0 GB of RAM, and a bundled NVIDIA L4 GPU with 24 GB of VRAM. It includes no local storage or complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Synthetic benchmarks reveal modest CPU performance, with Geekbench single-core and multi-core scores placing in the bottom quartile, alongside average memory bandwidth of 50.64 GB/sec uncached reads. In contrast, the accelerator delivers top-tier LLM inference performance, reaching 2,225.82 prompt tokens per second and 52.31 generation tokens per second on 7B parameter models. This configuration offers high resource efficiency for inference pipelines, graphics processing, and video transcoding, though it represents a poor tradeoff for storage-bound or CPU-heavy workloads.
